summary: A one-knob, config-only probe (S 16 -> 32 at sliding batch-1 decode) on the one shape master routes to _sliding_fused_kernel. The arithmetic checks out: chunk = ceil(2047/32) rounded to 64 = 64, so there is one tile per program and 32*64 >= 2047. Correctness risk is low because the -inf-safe combine and empty-chunk handling already exist. The expected headline effect (~0.8%) is below run drift, so judge it on the kernel row, not the headline.
justification: Mechanism: at B=1 the fused kernel is latency-bound, not bandwidth-bound. It moves 512 KB in 10.3 us (~0.05 TB/s, floor 0.1 us) on 32 CTAs of 132 SMs. Each program runs a dependent chain: q load, norm/rope, then per tile a page-table load, a dependent K/V gather, the dot and the online update, then the partial store, fence, ticket and combine. Halving the per-program tile chain from 2 to 1 dependent page-table+gather step should save roughly one gather latency (~1-1.5 us). Doubling CTAs to 64 still underfills the GPU, so there is no occupancy downside. FINDINGS supports this: the shape is 13.9 us with _sliding_fused_kernel 10.3 us at 100% of the kernel time, and ~3.6 us of the shape is graph/launch overhead that this change cannot touch. The expected directions match TASK.md: sliding decode_1 has weight 46, and the decode_1 load is ~46*13.9 + 16*27.9 ~= 1085 us. Saving ~1.2 us is ~5% on that load and ~0.8% on the 6-load geomean, inside the >=1.5% CI and inside observed drift. Byte-identical sliding decode_1 rows were 13.12, 13.22 and 13.88 us across three runs. The full / batch>1 / verify 'flat' expectations are correct, because the gate is cfg batch==1 and q_len==1 only. WEAKEST LINK: the '~1.5-1.8 us per tile' cost comes from sliding-single-launch-fused-attention's 2/8/16 tiles -> 13.5/23.9/38.5 us. Those three points are three different batches (1/16/32), CTA counts (32/128/128) and byte volumes (0.5/8/16 MB), not a within-shape sweep. With num_stages=2, Triton's pipeliner may already overlap the second tile's page-table/gather with the first tile's math, so the real saving may be well under 1.5 us. The second-weakest link is the combine cost. The last-ticket CTA alone serially reads 32 partials of [16,64] fp32 acc plus m/l (~135 KB vs ~68 KB at S=16; half of it is padding rows 8..15, which are stored and reloaded unmasked) through L2 with .cg. On a single SM that is plausibly +0.3-0.7 us of serial tail, not the stated +0.3 us. Expect -0.3 to -1.2 us on the kernel row. A null result is plausible and still informative: it says split depth is settled at B=1.
confounders: sliding-fused-triton-decode1-gate (landed): this is the kernel and gate being tuned. It is the parent's own code, not a confounder. Because the comparison is against master itself (S=16), the delta is attributable to S alone.

full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv (landed, current master): it does not touch the sliding path. It does load a load_inline CUDA module and run a self-check at import. Sliding decode_1 read 13.88 us under it vs 13.12 under the previous master with an unchanged kernel (10.5 -> 10.3 us kernel), so the shape row on this base already carries ~0.7 us of non-kernel drift. Compare kernel rows (_sliding_fused_kernel us) to master's 10.3 us, not shape rows to older runs.
fused-preattention-triton / paired-heads-* / fa3-hdim128-head-pairing (landed): no interaction. Batch-1 sliding decode bypasses _pre_attention_kernel and FA3 entirely on master.
interference: No companion is warranted. The run's own parent is master, which already runs the identical kernel at S=16, so this single run is the A/B of S=32 vs S=16 on one shape. No landed hypothesis's tuning changes what S does on this path. A control isolating a sub-change has nothing to isolate: the change is one constexpr (the optional runtime-range combine loop is an implementation detail, and keeping tl.static_range(32) is simpler and fine). Read the outcome from _sliding_fused_kernel's profile row against master's 10.3 us. Triton rows reproduce within ~1%, so a kernel delta of >=0.3 us is resolvable even though the headline is not. If it is flat or slower, the likely cause is the serial 32-way combine. A follow-up (not a companion) could mask the combine's workspace stores/loads to rvalid rows (halving the combine bytes) or move to a tree/parallel combine. Coordination note: the queued sibling sliding-deep-splits-on-cuda-splitkv (p1) edits the same `splits =` line and widens the gate to every decode batch with 16 splits. Write this change as an explicit override, e.g. `splits = 32 if batch == 1 and length == 1 else _num_splits(batch, hkv)`, so that the two still 3-way merge, and so that the sibling's 'S=16 for decode' does not silently undo S=32 at B=1 or vice versa.
rules_flags: None. S comes from config only (batch, q_len), with no value-dependent branching or allocation. ws_acc/ws_ml are torch.empty per call with config-derived shapes (graph pool). The ticket counters are the existing zeroed workspace sized B*Hkv and are independent of S, so nothing changes there. Every key in the window is still scored, since 32 chunks of 64 cover all 2047 old keys plus the new key on split S-1. There are no host syncs.

Correctness note for a scored submit: the only test that hits this path is 'batch 1, ctx 10, heads tp8, layer sliding' (page 64). At S=32, chunks 1..31 are empty (start > seq, the range loop does not execute) and write m=-inf, l=0. The new keys live on split S-1=31, so m_max is finite and empty partials get weight 0. This path is already exercised at S=16 and passes, so the risk is low. Confirm that the kernel compiles without spills at the larger unrolled combine (32 x [16,64] .cg loads) by checking the log or n_spills, if available.
open_questions: Does Triton's num_stages=2 pipeliner already overlap the 2nd tile's page-table load and gather at S=16? If so, the saving per removed tile is far less than the 1.5-1.8 us inferred from cross-batch data. The kernel row answers this.

Is the last-ticket combine (one CTA, serial 32 partials, ~135 KB incl. padding rows) now the dominant tail? If S=32 is flat, consider masking partial stores/loads to rvalid (8 of 16 rows) before trying any deeper split.
The sliding decode_1 shape row is ~3.6 us above the kernel (13.9 vs 10.3 us). That overhead (workspace allocs, graph node cost) is untouched here and may be a bigger lever than split depth.
